setup: TiO2 photocatalysts harvest mainly UV light, so sunlight-driven rapid disinfection with TiO2 is weak

steps.output: Er0.5Ti-O up-converts NIR excitation into green (520-570 nm) and red (640-690 nm) emission, stronger than Er0.75Ti-O ; Ce co-doping narrows the optical band gap of TiO2 from 2.90 eV to 2.20-2.46 eV, smallest (2.20 eV) at Ce 0.2
steps.output_short: Er0.5Ti-O up-converts NIR excitation into green (520-570 nm) and red (640-690 nm) emission, stronger than Er0.75Ti-O
steps.question: What does the evidence below show about the optical property?
observations: Emission in 520-570 nm (a) and 520-570 plus 640-690 nm (b) is ~3x (a) and ~7x (b) stronger for Er0.5Ti-O than Er0.75Ti-O
Co-doped absorption edges extend well past 420 nm into the visible vs a sharp TiO2 edge near 410 nm; Ce0.2 absorbs most
Tauc intercepts: TiO2 2.90, Er0.5Ce0.1 2.46, Er0.5Ce0.2 2.20, Er0.5Ce0.3 2.32 eV

steps.output: Under simulated sunlight for 20 min, Er0.5Ce0.2Ti-O kills ~91% of S. aureus and ~93% of E. coli vs ~45% for TiO2
